# Web project instructions

React 19 single-page app built with Vite 8.

## Stack and generated files

- TanStack Router owns file-based routes under `src/routes/`; route modules are page-layer components.
- `src/routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by `@tanstack/router-plugin`, committed, and never hand-edited.
- TanStack Query owns server state. Zustand stores under `src/stores/` own client UI state.
- Tailwind CSS v4 and daisyUI v5 are configured CSS-first in `src/styles.css`; there is no `tailwind.config.js`.
- The only theme is the light `workspace-light` daisyUI theme.

## Component boundaries

- Use functional components, named exports, and `FooProps` interfaces.
- Co-locate `Foo.tsx`, `Foo.test.tsx`, and `Foo.stories.tsx`.
- Follow atomic design: routes/pages → templates → organisms → molecules → atoms. Dependencies point downward; unrelated components in the same layer do not cross-import.
- Route modules own route params, TanStack Query hooks, and real data. Lower component layers stay presentational and receive props.
- Shared framework-agnostic helpers belong in `src/lib/`.
- Keep one configured relative HTTP client. Browser code never calls storage, LLM, or third-party API endpoints directly; route such calls through the backend and update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Styling and accessibility

- Prefer daisyUI component classes, then Tailwind utilities for layout and gaps.
- Use daisyUI semantic theme tokens instead of component-level literal colors.
- Do not add another component library, CSS framework, or Tailwind plugin without an approved documented reason.
- Preserve `className` pass-through on shared wrappers and prefer relative units except for one-pixel borders, shadow offsets, and media-query breakpoints.
- Use the `building-components`, `frontend-design`, and `web-design-guidelines` skills when their focused guidance applies.

## Tests and stories

Run commands from the repository root.

- Follow RED, GREEN, REFACTOR for behavior changes.
- Use Vitest and Testing Library; assert rendered behavior and user interactions, not private implementation details.
- Mock the API client boundary rather than internal component modules.
- Each story runs as a Chromium browser test. A story `play` function is an interaction test; import `expect`, `fn`, `userEvent`, and `within` from `storybook/test`.
- `nx test web` runs unit and Storybook browser projects and enforces 85% coverage.

## Commands

Install the browsers before running commands that exercise Storybook or E2E: `nx test web` and `nx e2e web-e2e` require them. Run commands from the repository root.

```bash
pnpm exec playwright install             # all browsers for web-e2e; Chromium is used by Storybook tests
pnpm exec nx serve web
pnpm exec nx build web
pnpm exec nx test web
pnpm exec nx typecheck web
pnpm exec nx lint web
pnpm exec nx storybook web
pnpm exec nx e2e web-e2e
```
